title: Keep amounts and fees apart in the ledger's sets

blocks.text: The payments ledger keeps its entries in hash sets and looks them up with `contains`. A refund of 2.50 CHF and a 2.50 CHF card surcharge are different entries, but reconciliation keeps losing one of them, and only on some days: it depends on which of the two was recorded first.
`Fee` extends `Amount` and adds a reason. Write both `equals` methods in `src/main/java/practice/Ledger.java`, so that:

items: two amounts are equal when their cents and currency are;
two fees are equal when their cents, currency and reason are;
an amount and a fee are never equal, whichever of the two is asked.

blocks.text: `hashCode` is already written. About six lines in total.

cases.says: two amounts with the same cents and currency are equal, and a set keeps one
amounts that differ in cents or in currency are not equal
two fees with the same cents, currency and reason are equal, and a set keeps one
fees for the same money and different reasons are not equal, asked either way
an amount is not equal to a fee of the same money, and a list of fees doesn't contain it
a fee is not equal to an amount of the same money, and a set keeps both
an amount compared with null is not equal and doesn't throw

origin.section: In equals, instanceof Breaks Symmetry With a Subclass, and getClass() Refuses Every Subclass

concepts: When a subclass adds state, instanceof in both equals methods breaks symmetry, so a collection's answer depends on which object it holds; getClass() keeps the classes apart.
